transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Aisha Gomez (Redwood SE), Omar Khan (Moraine CTO), Daniel Wu (VP Eng), Lina Morales (SRE)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on Private/VPC deployment options. Customer is evaluating Redwood Private behind their AWS VPC (primary region us-east-1) with strict egress controls and SOC2 requirements. Discussed VPC peering vs PrivateLink (interface endpoints), network architecture, CIDR/route table constraints, and next steps for pilot.

Topics:
- Private deployment topology (VPC peering, endpoints, NAT/egress)
- Regions and residency (primary us-east-1, DR in us-west-2, possibility of eu-west-1 for EU data)
- Security: SOC2, audit logs, KMS/HSM, SSO
- Networking specifics: CIDR, port 443, NAT, ENIs, private endpoints, cross-account peering
- Pilot scope and timeline

Transcript:
15:30 Speaker 1 (Samir): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intros, i'll hand to Aisha to jump into the network questions but first can you confirm we're talking Private/VPC only?
15:31 Speaker 2 (Omar): Yeah, hi, Omar here. We need Redwood Private inside our AWS. Hosted API won't fly for regulated PII in our workflows.
15:31 Speaker 1 (Samir): Got it, thanks. Aisha?
15:31 Speaker 3 (Aisha): hi team, Aisha from Redwood SE. we'll cover the common topologies — we support VPC peering, VPC endpoints/private link, and an on-prem option if needed. quick question: what region and what VPC config are you looking at?
15:32 Speaker 4 (Daniel): We're primarily in us-east-1, with a DR in us-west-2. Compliance wants data to remain in us-east-1 unless we explicitly fail over. we also have a case for some EU data, but that's a separate project.
15:32 Speaker 3 (Aisha): okay makes sense. for Private we typically deploy a control plane (managed by Redwood) and a customer data plane inside your VPC — or we can do fully private control plane in customer-managed account for larger enterprise. Which model are you leaning toward?
15:33 Speaker 2 (Omar): We prefer control plane to be private too — basically zero public endpoints if possible. Can you do cross-account peering so control plane runs in Redwood account but only accessible via peering?
15:33 Speaker 3 (Aisha): yes, cross-account VPC peering is common. Alternatively we support Interface endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) so you get private ENIs and the traffic never traverses the public internet. each has tradeoffs: peering is simpler network-wise but requires route table config; PrivateLink gives more isolation and easier service advertisement across accounts but can cost more and requires NLBs on our side.
15:34 Speaker 5 (Lina): quick clarifying q — will we need NAT gateways? we lock down egress and prefer fixed egress IPs for outbound requests to our infra.
15:34 Speaker 3 (Aisha): good question. in most setups the data plane inside your VPC will make outbound calls for model downloads and metrics; we can support a restricted egress model. options: 1) you provide NAT with fixed Elastic IPs and we route through it; 2) we arrange for VPC endpoint to services (S3, ECR) in your account; 3) we can stage container images in a private repo in your account. we'll work with your infra team.
15:35 Speaker 4 (Daniel): so for model updates we need to ensure artifacts don't go over public internet. S3 access via VPC endpoint is preferred. Also encryption — KMS with our CMK?
15:35 Speaker 3 (Aisha): yes you can provide a customer-managed KMS key for at-rest encryption. we'll integrate with that for encrypting model cache and logs. HSM integration is possible but that's a deeper enterprise workflow.
15:36 Speaker 1 (Samir): also to call out SLAs — Dedicated/Private deployments can get SLA commitments; we'll include latency SLOs for your workload class when we size the cluster.
15:36 Speaker 2 (Omar): latency — we run low-latency inference calls from our main app in us-east-1. what's your typical p99 for embeddings or chat when hosted in same region?
15:36 Speaker 3 (Aisha): p99 varies by model size and GPU profile. for a medium-sized generation model on a 1-2 GPU pool in region we'd expect p99 in the 60-150ms range for short sequences; larger models higher. important to size and to use KV cache. we can run benchmarks during the pilot to match your SLA.
15:37 Speaker 5 (Lina): do you support VPC peering across accounts in different regions? we sometimes peer across us-east-1 to us-west-2 for DR traffic.
15:37 Speaker 3 (Aisha): peering is regional per AWS rules; cross-region peering is supported but has different latency and costs. many customers keep primary workloads in single region and use DR region with data replication. we can replicate model caches if needed but it's additional complexity.
15:38 Speaker 4 (Daniel): what's the onboarding network checklist we should prepare?
15:38 Speaker 3 (Aisha): we'll send a runbook but top items: CIDR ranges for the VPC(s), route table rules, security group egress/ingress allowed (typically port 443 for control plane and optional admin ports), NAT/elastic IPs if you require fixed egress, list of S3 buckets or ECR repos and whether you'll provide VPC endpoints, and any proxy or HTTP inspection gateway we need to account for.
15:39 Speaker 2 (Omar): firewall policy — we have deep packet inspection and TLS termination on a proxy. will that break the service?
15:39 Speaker 3 (Aisha): TLS interception will break certificate pinning unless you terminate and reissue certs. we prefer end-to-end TLS; if inspection is unavoidable we'll need to test. also note mTLS between control plane and data plane is supported for enhanced security.
15:40 Speaker 5 (Lina): audit logs — can we forward logs to our CloudWatch or S3? and can you keep a copy for troubleshooting?
15:40 Speaker 3 (Aisha): yes we support pushing logs to your CloudWatch or S3 via an IAM role. we also keep operational logs in Redwood control plane for debugging; access to those is controlled and can be exported for audits.
15:41 Speaker 1 (Samir): question on compliance docs — we have SOC2 and ISO. i'll share the latest certs. Omar, do you need a signed BAA or other contracts?
15:41 Speaker 2 (Omar): eventually yes, for PHI workflows we'll need BAA. right now it's discovery but we'd like to see the security docs first.
15:41 Speaker 1 (Samir): we'll include SOC2, an overview of encryption at rest/in transit, and an initial BAA template for legal to review.
15:42 Speaker 4 (Daniel): procurement timeline — we want a 2-week pilot to validate network and latency. then procurement will look at reserved capacity pricing. can you support a short-term reserved or trial config?
15:42 Speaker 3 (Aisha): yes, pilot is standard. for Dedicated/Private we can provision a small pool and have limited reserved options for pilot; pricing table will be in the follow-up.
15:42 Speaker 1 (Samir): ok to wrap — recap and next steps: i'll send security pack and SOC2; Aisha will send VPC peering diagram and terraform samples; Lina will gather CIDRs & firewall requirements; we'll target pilot week of 3/16. Anything else?
15:43 Speaker 2 (Omar): that covers it, thanks.
15:43 Speaker 5 (Lina): thanks, appreciate the run-through.
15:43 Speaker 3 (Aisha): thanks all, sending artifacts.
15:43 Speaker 1 (Samir): thanks, we'll follow up in email with attachments and scheduling link. bye.
